text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- The cabinet approved the 1997 central budget, projecting that the deficit would not exceed HUF 390 billion and the average inflation is projected to be 18 percent.
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs in New York met Bosnian President Alija Izetbegovic and Carl Bildt, the UN commissioner for Bosnia and foreign ministers of Croatia and Bosnia.
- The upper house of Romania's Parliament on Thursday ratified the Romanian-Hungarian basic treaty.

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn, Speaker of Parliament Zoltan Gal and MP Matyas Szuros have each rejected an allegation published in the daily Uj Magyarorszag that they were "agents" of internal security under the communist regime.
- The National Bank of Hungary announced that it will decrease the central bank's base interest rate by 1.5 per cent to 23 per cent as of October 1 in order to decrease inflation.
- The International Finance Corporation, a World Bank organ, may acquire a significant stake in the ailing bus manufacturer Ikarus, said the company's incoming president Gabor Szeles.
NEPSZABADSAG
- The American concern General Motors will open a new assembly facility in its Opel factory in Szentgotthard today.
- In two weeks' time, credit rating institute Standard & Poor will probably decide whether to improve Hungary's credit rating from the present to a higher category.
VILAGGAZDASAG

- The United Nations' Industrial Development Organisation will soon open an office in Miskolc to provide assistance to small and medium-sized companies, said Karoly Attila Soos, secretary of the Industry and Trade Ministry.
- The Ministry of Industry and Trade has worked out a proposal for the utilisation of ECU 1 million in aid from the EU's PHARE programme to boost Hungarian tourism.
- The food retail company Tisza Fuszert of Szeged requested the initiation of banktruptcy proceedings against itself.

- Hungaria Biztosito and AB Aegon lead the list of insurance companies, followed by Providencia, Nationale Nederlanden, Generali and OTP-Garancia, according to a report in the economic magazine Figyelo.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Leaders of the hotel chain Danubius will sign a contract today to purchase most of the hotel chain Hungaria Szalloda Rt. from the State Privatisation and Holding Co.
- After a HUF 12.5 billion surplus in July, the income of the State Privatisation and Holding Co. exceeded its expenditures by HUF 9 billion last month.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- The entire continent will be supplied with Panasonic VCRs and mini sound systems coming from a new plant opened this week at the electronics company Videoton in Szekesfehervar.
- Eight investors have submitted their bids for the first round of the tender called to sell 25 per cent of the Budapest water works Fovarosi Vizmuvek Rt.
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 327 4040
